idiom_name: decimal.Decimal in a frozen dataclass with a currency value object
implementation_notes: Python's standard library gives away the hard half: decimal.Decimal is exact base-10 arithmetic with a context precision (28 digits by default), explicit quantize(exp, rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN) and scaleb for exponent shifts, so a Money type only has to add currency identity and the checks the language cannot make. The idiomatic realization is a frozen (therefore hashable) dataclass holding a Decimal amount and a Currency value with __add__/__sub__ raising on mismatched currencies, __mul__ restricted to scalars, and an allocate(n) that hands the remainder out instead of dividing. The classic hand-written class stays justified when it keeps exactly those invariants, and py-moneyed is the library shortcut when ISO currency data and Babel-backed formatting are wanted.
pitfalls: Decimal(float) inherits the float's binary error, so amounts must be built from str or int (Decimal("0.1")).
The decimal context is thread-local: code that mutates getcontext().prec or its rounding silently changes results in other modules on the same thread.
quantize raises InvalidOperation when the rounded result has more digits than the context precision, so large totals need an explicit localcontext.
float and Decimal refuse to mix silently (TypeError), and sum() needs a Money zero as its start value to aggregate a list of amounts.
